program: Street health outreach and youth housing

what: The Night Ministry provides street health outreach and youth housing in Chicago.
Its case managers also connect people to public programs, documents and longer-term housing support.
The annual-work illustration includes short health effects and signed household resources, not public ER savings or a verified marginal donation.
strengths: Current local services and public alternatives are documented.
FY2025 reports health assessments and housing outcomes.
The original audit distinguishes the recipient from its controlled asset-management organization.
reservations: Assessments are not unique treated patients, and stable housing is not measured causal health or income.
Cash savings, utility, overlap and additionality remain judgment inputs.
Current gift-created capacity and unquantified portfolio channels remain unknown.

sections.what: Street care and youth housing operate locally. Pilsen, New City, South Shore, Howard and Forest Park are current outreach anchors inside the 13-county Chicago MSA. [Schedule](https://thenightministry.org/get-help/)
sections.monitoring: FY2025 reports 3,631 assessments and 216 people moving to or maintaining safer stable housing. The 983 claimed avoided ER visits are not verified QALYs or deaths prevented. Track distinct treated conditions, resolution, duration and utility, plus sustained housing against alternatives. [Annual report](https://thenightministry.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/The-Night-Ministry_FY2025-Annual-Report.pdf) Fresh October review also finds 5,400 overall individuals, 487 young people provided housing and 57,597 encounters. These counts are not added to assessments or housing outcomes as distinct beneficiaries. Housing transitions and maintenance are mixed; utility and otherwise-paid consumption were not measured.
sections.qualitative: The housing trial remains an external caution against automatic health gains. Current youth programs provide emergency shelter, meals, case management, family support and independent-living skills; these establish plausible consumption and job pathways, not measured earnings. Central earnings are zero as an explicit uncertainty judgment, with positive and negative cases. Medical and housing cash hypotheses reflect otherwise-paid consumption net of benefits, taxes and alternatives, not retail services, rent or claimed public ER costs.
sections.cost: Root freshly checked the FY2025 original audit: TNM-only expense $11,424,900 plus $173,327 netted direct event costs gives $11,598,227. The $580,512 recognized in-kind is already in expenses; the subsidiary is not added again. Annual work removes the separate .3 gift-financing multiplier, without proving marginal gift capacity. Clinical health uses judged distinct actionable episodes and incremental relief, plus finite housing morbidity; full aggregate .05 process harm persists when benefits fail. Household grouping is resource-only, not another haircut to clinical people. Conditional health is 2.879828, signed resources +.140508 and price about $38.40M per ten combined equivalents. Whole-recipient cost against selected channels is not whole-portfolio expected value; the program-only sensitivity is not a verified allocated gift cost.
sections.funding: Root fresh audited TNM-only revenue is $11,841,571, ending net assets $12,594,087 and restricted assets $3,636,346. Specific assistance $225,650 mixes uncertain cash/in-kind incidence; it is not automatically household income. Public shelter, clinics and benefits are alternatives. Central resource households derive from judged episode and household factors; housing households are maximally nested in the medical group, and changed subgroups jointly receive net medical $50 or housing $100 hypotheses with .5 positive overlap. All exposed households retain judged $5 net incremental access/time cost relative to alternatives, even failed benefits. Those are not measured savings, and no gross wages are counted. Housing, other work and food/clothing channels beyond this conditional ledger remain unknown, not zero. Distinct outside payer costs are sensitivities and must exclude recognized resources already included in C. Unrestricted gifts support the recipient; current expansion cost and capacity are unknown. The $15,000 baseline consumption level is a judgment rather than observed income; $10,000 and $30,000 sensitivities expose the normative resource bridge.

sources.title: Original FY2025 consolidated and consolidating audit

model.costScope: TNM-only whole expense plus netted direct event costs; controlled subsidiary not added again.
model.geographicAttribution: g=.98 judged MSA share based on local service anchors; no national spillover credited.
model.formula: Health=g*(N*k*a*u*T+positive-only housing overlap(H*h*w*D)-full harm)/(1+r)^delay. Household resources=.5*sum(people*discounted years*log(after/before)*geography), joint overlapping gains and full net costs; price10=10*C/(health+signed resources).
model.counterfactual: Public and other medical care/shelter/housing alternatives; a and h are separate outcome hypotheses. Annual work does not receive a separate marginal donor multiplier.
model.attribution: Clinical and resource gates are judged, not measured effects. Assumed maximum household cohort overlap and shared changed subgroup are not observed. Full process harm and access burdens survive benefit failure.
model.uncertainty: Weak clinical calibration. Utility and duration are judgments; trial supports housing but cautions against assuming clinical benefit. The central estimate is an illustrative scenario, not a calibrated expected value; favorable/poor scenarios are not statistical confidence bounds. Service location establishes eligibility, while modeled MSA residency shares remain unmeasured.
model.nativeOutcomes: FY2025 assessments3631; transitioned or maintained housing216; overall5400individuals and487housed youth are not additive unique outcomes.
